name: SkyWater Florida advanced packaging facility (Center for NeoVation)

parties.name: Osceola County, Florida
parties.note: Leases the Center for NeoVation to SkyWater under a January 2021 development agreement joined by the non-profit BRIDG, and is developing technology and education facilities on the same campus.

parties.name: IonQ
parties.note: Acquired SkyWater, which became a wholly owned IonQ subsidiary on 31 July 2026.

summary: An advanced packaging plant at the Center for NeoVation in Kissimmee, Osceola County, Florida, that SkyWater Technology took over in 2021 and runs under a public-private partnership with the county. It offers fan-out wafer-level packaging, silicon interposers and hybrid wafer bonding for wafers made by SkyWater and by other foundries. The building covers about 109,000 square feet, with roughly 36,000 square feet of cleanroom. SkyWater agreed to bring the plant to full production capacity within five years; in 2025 it installed and qualified production tools as the site ramped up, and it is seeking Trusted accreditation for the plant. SkyWater, including this site, became a wholly owned subsidiary of IonQ in July 2026, and IonQ's report for the quarter to September 2026 lists the plant as its foundry business's Florida packaging facility.

metrics.note: Within a building of about 109,000 square feet.

milestones.note: SkyWater added the county-owned Center for NeoVation to its operations in 2021 under its lease and development agreements with Osceola County and BRIDG; the date marks the start of SkyWater's operation of the existing plant, not the opening of a new building.
Production tools installed and qualified during the site's ramp, with about US$10.3 million of start-up costs.
IonQ completed its acquisition of SkyWater.

notes: The filings give no investment amount, capacity or production start date for the plant; the opening milestone marks the year SkyWater took over the existing, county-owned plant rather than a new building. Under the 2021 lease SkyWater must bring the plant to full production capacity within five years, run it at full capacity for 15 more years and then take ownership of the building (s1). A federal Build Back Better grant to Osceola County and BRIDG partly funds expansion and equipment at the plant, with SkyWater committed to a 20 percent matching share estimated at about USD 10.2 million at the end of 2025 (s1); the grant amount for the plant is not stated and is not recorded. The company field names IonQ, SkyWater's parent since July 2026.
